# motion-film

> motion-film is a free, open-source (MIT) Claude Code skill that turns a product, website or GitHub repo into a finished launch video, explainer, teaser or Instagram Reel, made fully in code and rendered locally with raea. It writes and scores the hook, records a local voice-over, builds the motion graphics, adds a sound to every on-screen action, checks the cut for slideshow pacing, and renders an MP4 with real motion blur. No After Effects, no video editor, no screen recording, no AI video model.

Install in Claude Code: `/plugin marketplace add s-azizkhan/motion-film-skill` then `/plugin install motion-film@motion-film`, then install raea (`curl -fsSL https://raea.io/install | sh`) and run the skill's `setup.sh`. Use: `/motion-film . "launch film" --format both`.

Runs on macOS (Apple Silicon), Linux x86_64 and Windows 10/11 with 16 GB RAM and about 5 GB of disk; optional local audio models add about 10 GB.

- [Toolkit reference](https://github.com/s-azizkhan/motion-film-skill/blob/main/docs/toolkit.md): filmcheck.py slideshow checker, shutter.sh motion blur, moves.ts motion library, sound pipeline, proven formats search
- [Examples](https://github.com/s-azizkhan/motion-film-skill/blob/main/docs/examples.md): a 9:16 launch Reel made with the skill
